text:
rachel: Heads up: customer A filed a ticket that after we turned on the v2 default routing, their invoices show a weird drop in v2 usage and a matching unexplained bump in v1. looks like route-affinity + fallback path are double-counting tokens.

omar: do we have a quick repro? or raw logs?

rachel: got a small sample from their tenant logs. sequence: client calls w/o version -> routing returns v2 but with header `x-rw-fallback: v1` present for compatibility. metrics pipeline counts both `served_via` and `fallback_route` signals.

jess: that `x-rw-fallback` header was only meant for debugging. bad that it leaks into telemetry.

pat: options: 1) strip debugging header before emitting telemetry 2) change ETL to dedupe when both signals share request_id 3) treat fallback as a non-billing tag.

rachel: quick fix preference? we need minimal runtime risk but also accurate billing.

omar: ETL dedupe (2) is safest operationally but slower to deploy. stripping header (1) is tiny change and rollbackable. making fallback non-billing (3) will change past numbers in reports.

jess: think about dashboards: internal SLO dashboards expect per-route split to tie to capacity. if we silently remove counts from v1 we may hide real fallback traffic that consumed v1 capacity. billing can't ignore it.

pat: good point. Another angle: add `attribution_request_id` to request lifecycle so both routing and cache/telemetry use the same canonical id; ETL can then decide canonical owner without double counting. medium-term work.

rachel: timeline suggestion: a) immediate: strip debug header from telemetry emitted (patch + canary) b) short: add attribution_request_id and backfill mapping c) medium: ETL rule to prefer the "final_served_route" field if present for billing.

infra-bot: Deploy scheduled: strip-tel-header-patch -> canary 5% in 5m.

omar: I'll implement strip + add logs showing pre/post counts. Jess, can you own the SRE alert to catch sudden v2 capacity drops?

jess: yep. will add pager rule: if v2 token rate drops > 15% vs baseline after deploy, notify eng-oncall.

billing-bot: FYI billing pipeline team: if we change canonical attribution, we'll need a short notice to finance and a migration plan for monthly reconciliations.

pat: for the attribution_request_id, we need to decide where it's minted. routing layer seems best since it decides variant. then propagate via context to cache + telemetry.

omar: agreed. I'll add a UUID field `rw_attr_id` to routing response and ensure cache writes include it. also add a small TTL so stale cache entries don't carry old attribution forever.

rachel: TTL note: some tenants rely on long-lived cached responses for speed. can we make TTL configurable per-tenant? if we change default we might bust their perf.

omar: default keep same, but for entries with rw_attr_id include `attr_expires_at` set to min(cache_ttl, 24h). That keeps attribution bounded.

jess: testers: create a smoke script to simulate: 1) call without version header 2) routing chooses v2 with rw_attr_id 3) cache hit later should show same rw_attr_id 4) telemetry aggregated should attribute to rw_attr_id owner.

rachel: communications: we should add a short console banner for tenants during rollout: "We're improving how we count traffic across versions. You may see temporary attribution shifts in billing. Contact support if billing looks incorrect." Keep it non-technical.

billing-bot: request accepted. finance wants a list of affected tenants before we flip to full rollout. Please tag any tenants with >1M tokens/day that saw >10% shift.

pat: last thought: for long-term UX, console should show a toggle: "Version attribution mode: route-based vs request-based" so tenants can preview how attribution affects their estimated monthly bill. but post-mvp.

omar: agree, add ticket to eng-product backlog.

rachel: owners: omar -> header strip + rw_attr_id propagation, pat -> ETL dedupe + final_served_route rule, jess -> SRE alerts + smoke tests, rachel -> comms + console banner copy, billing-bot -> finance sync. reconvene 48h. :thumbsup:
